For the filling: 1 cup of sugar 3 Tbsp of flour 3 cups of rhubarb (2-3 stalks) 3 cups of strawberries

For the crust: 1.5 cups of flour 1 cup of brown sugar 1 cup of butter (chilled, cubed) 1 cup of rolled oats

Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C)

Mix the filling ingredients in a bowl and set aside. (I have a huge sweet tooth, so I don't mind it with 1 cup of sugar, but if you want it to be less sweet, you can easily use less.)

Mix the ingredients for the crust until crumbly.

Put filling in a 9x13 baking pan. (I actually used a 9x9 to make it really thick.) Top with crust mixture. Bake for 45 minutes, or until crispy and the top is slightly browned.

I'm not a big fan of sugar, but I'm considering trying this with substituting some apple sauce in lue of sugar for the filling and possibly some oat flour or brown rice flour for the brown sugar. Looks delicious!

Also do you bake it on the middle rack in the oven?

Apple sauce sounds like a good alternative. Just something to help cut down on the tartness of the Rhubarb.

And yes, I baked it on the middle rack! I recommend putting another pan lined with baking parchment underneath in case the fruit bubbles up and drips over the edge like mine did, leaving burnt goo on the bottom of my oven.

Enjoy! I'd be curious to hear how it goes with those substitutions. :)

I posted this on the other site recently, and thought I would post it here too since I think many would benefit from listening the podcast below.

On my commute the other day, I listened to Leaving the Church: A Conversation with Megan Phelps-Roper the latest podcast from Waking Up with Sam Harris. You might recognise the 'Phelps' part of Megan's name - she was once a member of the Westboro Baptist Church. Sam's interview with her is very interesting, and they cover all sorts of areas, from the beginnings of the church, to the commencement of their infamous picketing, to the thing that led to Megan leaving.

As someone who has in the last couple of years left the highly controlling environment of the JWs, I really related to some of Megan's experiences. In the interview Megan made a comment that for me, with my experience, rang very true and I thought you guys might be able to relate. She mentioned a New York Times article called The Brain's Empathy Gap and it was a quote from that article that really struck me: "The suppression of empathy is most strongly correlated with group identity." She followed this up with the statement "The stronger your group identity the more you are able to suppress empathy for the outgroup."

Both comments are right on the money in my opinion. JWs encourage minimal contact with 'the world' and an 'us and them' mentality. As a group they look forward to Armageddon - the death of billions of people on earth, are not encouraged to donate to or assist charities, and unless there is potential for conversion, advised to not associate with those who are not part of the religion. This engenders a general lack of empathy - no need to worry about that thing or do anything about it, Armageddon will be here soon and God's Kingdom will fix everything.

The quoted article, and Megan's comments echo true with my personal experience.

Something else she quoted hit home too. From the book Journey to Jihad about a young guy who gets radicalised by Islam: "The threat of excommunication kept most members obedient." So very true. Lots of people stay with these groups, not because they love the religion, but because they fear being cut off from their social group and years of connections.

Near the end of the podcast, she speaks about when she actually left, and again there were many parallels with my (and I am sure many others) exit from the borg.

Very interesting. Anyway, I thought you guys might like it too. Here is the link.
Sam Harris - Leaving the Church (Interview with Megan Phelps-Roper, ex Westboro Baptist Church member)
